searchText: Hi everyone - the Besu team has written a post-mortem for our Mainnet halting event on January 6th. The details are at the link below: https://wiki.hyperledger.org/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=117440824 The 1000 foot view is that some create2/self-destruct patterns were being used in a way that exposed a corner case in our state DB implemenation. Correction I'm pretty sure most of you have seen my reddit post by now. Since it was getting more attention, I decided to run the numbers again and realized that they are pre-shanghai numbers. The attack relies heavily on behavior that is not possible anymore. Post-shanghai I get ~250ms on geth (down from 1.3s) On reth I get ~150ms (down from 6s) on besu ~2.7s (down from 8.2s) (on a different machine thanks to <@841775421024239688> ) I couldn't get the nethermind numbers unfortunately, but they should also be way less The current test case I have is not optimal, but should be close to the worst case possible under 40MGas. To reiterate, these numbers are WORST CASE numbers for a specific attack. These are not in any way indicative of the performance of a client under normal conditions. To note this also includes the JVM startup time on Besu, which will impact the overall time result - same with Netherminds VM and is not applicable to normal conditions for the Nodes. We will share some more numbers soon https://tenor.com/view/disappointed-dis-to-eli-gif-19145295 We were able to test this now at ~87ms We were able to reduce the numbers on besu to less then 100 ms by reducing startup time, use the same Java instance for multiple tests. The numbers we got are on MacBook Pro M1 (first gen). cc. <@403707149043105803> ```{"output":"","gasUsed":"0x2625a00","time":78640791,"Mgps":"508.642","test":"jd_attack_london_10MGas_JUMPDEST_250M","fork":"Shanghai","d":0,"g":0,"v":0,"postHash":"0xb477153913f9f4214202f0eda1fa4afe153f937dee736e6284bd188e71a63ae6","postLogsHash":"0x1dcc4de8dec75d7aab85b567b6ccd41ad312451b948a7413f0a142fd40d49347","pass":false} ```

Hi everyone - the Besu team has written a post-mortem for our Mainnet halting event on January 6th. The details are at the link below:

https://wiki.hyperledger.org/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=117440824

The 1000 foot view is that some create2/self-destruct patterns were being used in a way that exposed a corner case in our state DB implemenation.

The current test case I have is not optimal, but should be close to 
the worst case possible under 40MGas.

To reiterate, these numbers are WORST CASE numbers for a specific attack.
These are not in any way indicative of the performance of a client under 
normal conditions.
